A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RobotSeg and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary Sections 7–15. Their methods, equations, tables, figures, and appendix material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and video segmentation experiments, ablations, category-wise evaluations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative application results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports a fine-tuned RoboEngine comparator in Tables 2 and 3.

M1.justification: The memory associator, robot prompt generator, hierarchical clustering, consistency losses, and decoder remain unchanged. Revised Section 4.1 wording clarifies operations already documented in v1, including supplementary Section 14.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use RoboEngine and VRS with the same ten robot embodiments and whole-robot, arm, and gripper segmentation tasks. The supplementary application examples and test scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 add RoboEngine (Finetuned) alongside the retained original RoboEngine model. Other comparators remain unchanged; VideoLISA and SAM 3 were already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: Tables 2 and 3 introduce an additional fine-tuned RoboEngine training condition alongside the original model. Existing splits, metrics, prompting procedures, and RobotSeg training settings remain unchanged. The added comparator's fine-tuning procedure is unspecified.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 4, embodiment analysis in Tables 5–7, efficiency analysis in Table 8, and supplementary qualitative and application case studies are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Results continue to be presented as point estimates.

E6.justification: New fine-tuned RoboEngine results are 80.2 J&F on VRS and 86.6 on RoboEngine images; original-model scores remain 74.1 and 85.9. RobotSeg remains at 85.1 and 87.9. Section 5.2 revises the stated video margin from 11.0 to 4.9. Other results, including appendix results, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and losses are equivalent. v1's Equations 3–4 are grouped into v2's Equation 3, with subsequent renumbering; this introduces no new derivation, assumption, or formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about RobotSeg, the VRS benchmark, the three principal technical contributions, and state-of-the-art image and video segmentation.

C2.justification: Explanations concerning structural modeling, temporal consistency, domain adaptation, and embodiment generalization remain unchanged. Section 15 retains the same limitations concerning difficult robot categories and computational overhead.

D1.justification: The training schedule, optimizer settings, hardware, training time, architectural details, and repository link are retained. The new fine-tuned RoboEngine rows provide no additional implementation or training recipe.

R1.justification: v2 adds SAMi2V++ as reference 38 in the promptable video segmentation discussion while retaining SAMi2V. Other reference changes concern bibliographic corrections or formatting, without substantive repositioning.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the memory-associator explanation, corrects grammatical errors and the RPG reference from Figure 7 to Figure 6, adds figure-panel references, and includes funding acknowledgments. The section sequence and overall narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 is reorganized, Tables 2–3 gain comparator rows, and supplementary tables are reformatted. Figure 5 gains variable and operation labels. Resizing and spacing changes keep the abstract on page 1 and the conclusion on page 8.

improvement.justification: Adding the fine-tuned RoboEngine comparator makes the competitive evidence more informative: RobotSeg's automatic video advantage over it is 4.9 J&F, compared with 11.0 over the original comparator. Corrected references and clearer displays also improve readability. The new comparator's fine-tuning procedure remains unspecified, limiting the evidential gain.
